newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks worry about falling credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks worry about falling credit ratings.

text.p: South Korean banks said on Wednesday they expected their credit ratings would be downgraded as a result of continuing corporate failures.
Standard & Poor's Corp said it had placed five South Korean banks on Credit Watch with negative implications.
"We already anticipated that, but we can do nothing about it," said Kim Yoon-sang, an official in Korea First Bank's international financing division.
An official at Korea Exchange Bank said the announcement indicated a downgrade was likely.
"It looks like the credit-rating company is considering raising South Korea's country risk as a whole," he said.
The five banks were Hanil Bank, Korea Exchange Bank, Korea First Bank, Korea Long-Term Credit Bank and Shinhan Bank.
The five banks plus Kookmin Bank were the only South Korean banks now rated by S&P.
"South Korean banks' credit ratings would likely be lowered in the short-term because companies and banks should undergo restructuring," said Lee Hahn-koo, president of Daewoo Research Institute.
"But South Korea traditionally guarantees the safety of banks. The government will come up with some measures to reduce risks in the banking industry," Lee said.

S&P said its action reflected the deteriorating asset quality and heightening industry risks faced by South Korean banks as defaults continue to emerge among Korea's highly leveraged industrial conglomerates.
It said it is concerned about the potential for spillover of defaults to other sectors of the economy and ultimately to the banking sector.
The overall deterioration in asset quality in Korea has recently been demonstrated by the Kia crisis, S&P said.
"It is another blow to the banking sector, which is already suffering from the Kia Group's troubles," said Koo Kyong-hoi, analyst at Dongwon Economic Research Institute.
